archetype.name: Dual-Threat (veteran backup)
archetype.definition: A 12-year veteran QB2 who wins with accurate short throws and well-timed designed runs rather than arm talent, and who has always been a capable fill-in with a mid-pack ceiling.

report.headline: Efficient fill-in on 57 dropbacks, now hurt and buried behind Daniels
report.take:
Mariota is what he has been for a decade: a functional, accurate, mobile quarterback who keeps an offense on schedule without lifting it. This season he has been Washington's emergency option. He relieved in Week 2 at 45% of snaps, played all of Week 3 in a win over Seattle, then made his only start in Week 4 and was gone after 16% of the snaps. He is now out with an MCL sprain and listed as QB2 behind Jayden Daniels, who started the last two games. The only real question is what he gives the offense if he is needed again.

The efficiency line looks better than his career says it should: 0.21 EPA per dropback (11th of 45), a 7.8% TD rate (4th) and no interceptions. Most of that value comes from the short game. Throws under 10 air yards ran 0.248 EPA on a 77.8% completion rate, 7.5 points over expected, which fits his history. His CPOE sat at 3.2 last year and 3.45 in 2018. Past 10 yards he completed a third of his throws. Three of his four TDs came on those attempts, and they are the fragile part of the line.

The numbers also hide game script. When trailing by nine or more he posted 0.604 EPA a play on 12 plays. In one-score situations he was at -0.014. On third down he was at -0.276 and converted 26.7%. Strip out the catch-up snaps against soft coverage and he looks like an average passer, which is his career norm: his EPA per play has never ranked higher than 15th. He was also pressured on 38.9% of dropbacks, the most of anyone qualifying, behind a line that ranks 27th in hits allowed. Yet he took sacks on only 14.3% of pressures. Every prior charted season he ran above 31% on that rate, so expect it to regress to his long-standing tendency to hold the ball and absorb sacks.

From here it is a waiting role. He is targeting a November 1 return, and Terry McLaurin, his most productive target, carries the same date with a knee injury. When Mariota is healthy and Daniels is not, expect a capable, low-turnover game manager with real rushing value on designed keepers. Do not expect the 0.21 EPA pace on a full workload.

strengths.title: Accurate, efficient short passing
strengths.body: He completed 76.7% of throws in the 0-9 yard range, 8.9 points over expected, and those throws carried most of his passing value. It is a skill he has shown for years, with positive CPOE last season and in 2018, so it is the most bankable part of his game in any spot start.

strengths.title: Designed runs still produce
strengths.body: Both designed runs succeeded, including a 35-yard rushing day in his abbreviated Week 4 start. Two plays is a tiny sample. Still, he has ranked inside the top 13 QBs in rushing yards in five of his seven listed seasons, so the legs are a durable part of his value, the MCL sprain aside.

strengths.title: Ball security so far
strengths.body: He has zero interceptions and zero turnover-worthy plays on 51 attempts, after averaging 0.78 interceptions a game last season. Part of that is caution: his aggressiveness fell from 19.8% to 14.89%. It is a real stylistic shift toward checkdowns, but 51 attempts cannot establish that he has stopped throwing picks.

concerns.title: Value inflated by catch-up snaps
concerns.body: Trailing by nine or more he was excellent. In one-score games he was roughly break-even, and on third down he was clearly negative. The headline EPA leans on plays where defenses concede the underneath. In a competitive start, expect something closer to league average.

concerns.title: Sack avoidance won't hold
concerns.body: He faced the heaviest pressure rate of any qualifier, yet turned only 14.3% of pressures into sacks. That rate ranked 3rd, after years ranking 33rd to 52nd. Behind a line that allows hits at a bottom-six rate, more of those pressures will become sacks and stalled drives.

concerns.title: Deep TDs on a 25% hit rate
concerns.body: Two touchdowns on eight deep attempts, with only two completions, is a TD rate that will not repeat. His deep CPOE was -8.8, and losing McLaurin removes the target who produced most of his passing value.

trend.note: His usage swung from 45% of snaps in Week 2 to 100% in Week 3 to 16% in his Week 4 start. He has not appeared since Daniels returned in Week 5, and he is now sidelined with an MCL sprain.

nextGame.headline: Likely inactive or holding a clipboard against a soft Eagles front
nextGame.body:
If he plays, the Philadelphia matchup suits him. The Eagles rank last in QB hit rate and 31st in sack rate, which would ease the pressure that hounded him. They also allow 0.54 EPA a target to opposing WR1s, among the worst in the league. The catch is that they rank 9th against deep passes, which matters little for a passer who lives under 10 yards anyway.

Availability decides everything. Mariota is out with a knee sprain and an estimated return of November 1, game day itself, and he sits behind Daniels on the depth chart. McLaurin is also out with a knee injury through the same date. On Philadelphia's side, edge rushers Jalyx Hunt and Nolan Smith Jr. are out or questionable, and slot corner Michael Carter II is out. Those absences would further soften a pass rush that already rarely gets home. No line or total is posted yet.

keyMatchups.title: Weak Eagles pass rush
keyMatchups.body: Philadelphia hits quarterbacks at the lowest rate in the league, and two of its edge rushers are on the report. For a passer who was pressured more than any qualifier, that is the single biggest relief this matchup could offer.

keyMatchups.title: WR1 room without McLaurin
keyMatchups.body: The Eagles bleed production to opposing No. 1 receivers. With McLaurin out, that role falls to Stefon Diggs, whose 0.072 EPA per target from Mariota was far less productive.

nextGame.watch: Whether he is activated off the knee injury at all, and whether Daniels' health ever forces him back into the lineup.

restOfSeason.body:
As a healthy QB2, Mariota's expected weekly line is close to zero. His value is as insurance, and that insurance is decent: an accurate short passer who rarely turns it over and can steal yards on designed keepers. If he starts, expect something like 170 to 230 passing yards and around one TD a game, plus a rushing floor. He may also have less mobility than usual coming off an MCL sprain.

What regresses: the 7.8% TD rate, the deep touchdowns on a 25% completion rate, and the unusually low pressure-to-sack rate. All three run against his career profile. What holds: short-area accuracy, the lean toward conservative reads, and the scramble and keeper value. Washington's offense is middling, and his top target is out, so a fill-in stint would likely look average rather than like the EPA rank he carries now.

confidence.note: Only 57 dropbacks across three games, a current knee injury, and a backup role that hinges on Daniels' health.
